subject: Granular inference metrics & telemetry — roadmap check-in
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com, eng@cloudops.com
Date: 2027-11-01T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Granular inference metrics & telemetry — roadmap check-in

Team —

Short ask: can we scope a narrow, incremental roadmap to deliver truly queryable, per-route token cost and latency telemetry by model-variant so we can quickly answer tenant incidents (Acme) and support per-customer SLA investigations? Current console slices are helpful at a surface level, but the recent outage showed we lack a) per-model-variant breakdown (fp16 vs q4 vs q4_0), b) token-level cost attribution for expensive reranking calls, and c) easy filtering by tenant + path for tail p95/p99 analysis.

What I need for this week: a realistic proposal (3 bullets max) that includes a minimal first step we can ship in a canary, estimated engineering effort (T-shirt size), and any storage/retention cost implications. Acme has asked for an ETA because they have a SOC-style postmortem coming up.

Constraints to keep in mind: retention should be configurable by route, retention default should be 7 days for the canary; avoid increasing per-token serving overhead more than 3–5%.

Why this matters: being able to answer \"which model variant + route + tenant produced these expensive tokens and why\" will reduce ops MTTR and enable smarter routing/caching suggestions in Optimize.

Attachments: rough sketch of metrics we talked about (route-metrics-sketch.png).

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Product Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@cloudops.com
Date: 2027-11-02T11:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Granular inference metrics & telemetry — roadmap check-in

Jonas —

I sketched a pragmatic, low-risk incremental approach that keeps runtime overhead small:

1) Per-request metadata tagging (route, tenant_id, model_variant, quantization_tag) emitted at ingest and attached to existing token/latency event streams. No change to inference pipeline, just add tags. Lightweight.

2) Windowed aggregation service (lambda-style) that consumes streams and writes per-route/day/1h aggregates plus p50/p90/p95/p99 latency histograms and token-cost counters into a columnar store. This gives us fast rollups for console tiles without storing every token.

3) Optional sampled trace capture: for top X% of requests by token-cost or latency we capture full trace (KV cache hits, prompt length, decoding steps). Stored separately behind a TTL.

T-shirt sizes: 1) S, 2) M, 3) M-L.

Notes/risks: need to decide sample rate (we typically do 0.1–1% for traces). We also need a short list of routes to include in the canary (suggest: /chat, /re-rank, /batch-embed). CloudOps: if you can confirm streaming tags are OK on your side, we'll be able to push the event producer change in one sprint.

Attaching my sketch for the aggregation shape (route-metrics-sketch.png).

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior SWE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-11-03T14:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Granular inference metrics & telemetry — roadmap check-in

Thanks Grace — this incremental plan looks good. A couple of product-level asks to make sure the canary is useful for customers and CS: 

- Console UX: we should provide a queryable table (time-range + route + model_variant + tenant filter) and an export CSV button. The minimum viable tile is: p95 latency, p99 latency, avg token-cost, requests, sample traces link.
- RBAC: only CS and tenant owners should be able to see per-tenant traces. Default tile visibility to admin orgs.
- Retention: for the canary keep full histograms for 14 days (configurable later), sampled traces for 7 days.
- Alerting: expose an API to create SLO alerts based on p99 latency and token-cost spikes. We can wire this into existing alerting infra.

Can we aim for a 6-week canary owned by Observability (Jonas) + Serving (Grace) with a Console PM UX drop by week 3? Marcus — can you validate storage cost delta for the aggregation approach (expected: low, columnar storage, estimate to follow).

I attached a mock of an initial tile (mock-console-v2.fig).

Kimberly Park
Product Manager, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Pablo Ruiz <ops@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-05T08:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Granular inference metrics & telemetry — roadmap check-in

Jonas / Kimberly —

Appreciate the outreach. We had a big cost spike on Nov 3 during a scheduled batch rerank that impacted our SLA window. Support ticket: ACME-2027-1103 (https://support.acmehealth.com/tickets/ACME-2027-1103). If you can accelerate the canary to include our tenant and /re-rank route, that would be ideal — we need to present evidence in our postmortem to our compliance team next week.

Questions from our side: 1) will any PII be captured in sampled traces? 2) can sampled traces be scoped to only non-production IDs? 3) ETA for a first readout?

— Pablo Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops
Acme Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com, eng@cloudops.com
Date: 2027-11-07T15:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Granular inference metrics & telemetry — roadmap check-in

Team — summary and concrete next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Scope (canary): per-request tags + 1h aggregates for routes: /chat, /re-rank, /batch-embed. Include per-model-variant breakdown (fp16, q4, q4_0). Tenant-level filter enabled; sampled traces enabled for top 0.5% by token-cost. (Owner: Grace) — target ship to internal canary infra in 6 weeks (2027-12-19).

2) Console: initial queryable tile (p95/p99/avg token-cost/requests) + CSV export + link to sampled traces (RBAC: admin/org-level only). UX drop by week 3 (mock attached). (Owner: Kimberly) — week 3 demo planned 2027-11-22.

3) Storage/Cost: Marcus to provide delta estimate for 14d histograms + sampled traces. If cost > 2x baseline, we will reduce histogram retention to 7 days for the canary. (Owner: Marcus) — estimate by 2027-11-12.

4) Customer acceleration: Pablo (Acme) — we will include Acme in the canary if they sign the canary addendum (minimal data handling clauses) and confirm no PII in sampled traces. Grace will provide an export that redacts user identifiers by default. (Owner: Jonas + Legal) — target agreement by 2027-11-15.

Links & artifacts: HubSpot contact: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-12345, Jira ticket: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/RED-9876. Attached starter runbook (runbook_starter.md) and the sketches mentioned earlier.

If everyone agrees, I'll create the Jira epic and invite owners.

Thanks —
Jonas
